Location: Florida's Atlantic coast – Fernandina Beach to Jupiter Inlet (coastal waters 0–60 nm), with a gale watch Jupiter Inlet to Ocean Reef
Item: UPDATE: Gale watch upgraded to gale warning – Fernandina to Jupiter Inlet, through Monday evening
Details: Yesterday's gale watch is now a gale warning. NWS Jacksonville: Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine, NE winds 25–35 kt, gusts to 40 kt, seas 8–13 ft (9–14 ft offshore), until 8pm EDT Mon Oct 26; St. Augustine to Flagler Beach from 3pm Sat. NWS Melbourne: Flagler Beach to Sebastian Inlet from 8pm Sat, Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet from 8am Sun – NE 20–30 kt, gusts to 35 kt, seas 10–15 ft, until 8pm EDT Mon. NWS Miami: gale watch Jupiter Inlet to Ocean Reef from Sun afternoon through at least Mon evening (NE 20–30 kt, gusts 35, seas 9–14 ft possible). Why it matters: a strong northeaster against the Gulf Stream makes every Atlantic inlet from Fernandina to Jupiter dangerous for sailboats and small cruisers, and the ICW itself will be gusty and choppy across the open stretches.
When: Sat Oct 24 – 8pm EDT Mon Oct 26 2026 (start times vary by zone)
Notes: What to do: stay inside – no outside passages or inlet runs this weekend. If you're moving south on the ICW, plan short hops and secure the boat early; double up lines and add chafe gear for a multi-day northeaster. NWS: 'Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the vessel.' Check back Monday evening for the end of the warning – the NWS offshore forecast keeps NE 20–25 kt into midweek. Location pin is a representative point near Ponce Inlet. Updates the 2026-10-23 gale-watch row.

Location: Miami Marine Stadium Harbor, Virginia Key (Biscayne Bay, Miami)
Item: Powerboat-race safety zone closes Miami Marine Stadium Harbor through Sunday
Details: Coast Guard temporary safety zone for the Luminsea Miami Shootout and Races covers all waters of Miami Marine Stadium Harbor, 10am–11:59pm daily Oct 22–25. No entry without Captain of the Port permission; about 60 race boats and 50 spectator craft expected. Why it matters: the Marine Stadium basin is a popular anchorage and rafting spot off the Rickenbacker Causeway – it's off-limits through Sunday night.
Notes: What to do: anchor elsewhere (e.g. off Key Biscayne or Dinner Key) until Monday. To request entry: VHF 16 or (833) 642-7271. Questions: MST2 Elliot Cortes, Sector Miami Waterways Management, 786-295-9051. Same weekend as the gale watch for Miami's coastal waters (Sun–Mon).

Location: Colorado River Locks, near Matagorda (GIWW mile 441.5)
Item: Colorado River Lock daytime repair closures scheduled to end Oct 23
Details: The weekday 8am–6pm closures of the Colorado River Lock for West Lock sector-gate repairs were scheduled from Aug 19 through Oct 23. ACBL's barge-industry report (updated Oct 23) still lists that end date; no reopening notice from the Corps found yet. Why it matters: if the work wrapped on time, the daily 10-hour wait on this stretch of the Texas GIWW is gone – on Oct 23 tows were still averaging 12 hours of delay, so recreational boats should expect a backlog to clear first.
When: Closure window Aug 19 – Oct 23 2026 (reopening not confirmed)
Notes: What to do: call the Lockmaster before you plan around it – (979) 863-7842 ext. 2002 or government cell (979) 482-7321 (numbers from a 2025 Corps notice; may have changed). Uncertainty: this is the scheduled end date, not a confirmed reopening; an Oct 1 Celtic Marine report said 'no ETA to reopen.' Brazos River Floodgates restrictions (mile 401) continue through Dec 28.

Location: Sarasota Sailing Squadron, 1717 Ken Thompson Pkwy, City Island, Sarasota (Sarasota Bay)
Item: Great Pumpkin Regatta at Sarasota Sailing Squadron
Details: Sarasota Sailing Squadron's Halloween-season Great Pumpkin regatta on Sarasota Bay. Why it matters: the Squadron sits on City Island by New Pass, so the racing is easy to watch from shore.

Location: Davis Island Yacht Club, 1315 Severn Ave, Tampa (Hillsborough Bay)
Item: A-Class Catamaran World Championship comes to Tampa
Details: Davis Island Yacht Club hosts the 2026 A-Class Catamaran Worlds (Regatta Network: Nov 7–14; class site: Nov 9–14), with the Admiral's Cup warm-up regatta just before (listed Nov 4). The A-Class is a single-handed racing catamaran class. Why it matters: world-championship racing right off downtown Tampa – and a busy DIYC run of events, right after the Star North Americans.
Notes: What to do: plan for race-course traffic on Hillsborough Bay those days; Davis Islands is the best shore-side vantage. Date nuance: Regatta Network lists Nov 7–14 for the Worlds; the class site said Nov 9–14 racing with an Admiral's Cup warm-up Nov 5–6 – exact race days not confirmed. Same club also lists the Sailing Sisters Regatta on Nov 7.
